# 1 Chronicles Chapter 28 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 384v–385r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_028_page_001.jpg, 1CH_028_page_002.jpg

---

**1** David summoned all the leaders of Israel to Jerusalem — the tribal officials, the divisional commanders who served the king, the military officers of every rank, the administrators of the royal properties and herds, the court officials, the warriors, and every man of standing.

**2** King David stood up and addressed them: "Listen to me, my brothers and my people. I had it in my heart to build a permanent home for the ark of the LORD's covenant — a resting place for the footstool of our God — and I made plans to build it. **3** But God told me, 'You are not to build a house for my name, because you are a warrior who has shed blood.'

**4** "Still, the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me out of my entire family to be king over Israel forever. He chose the tribe of Judah to lead, and from Judah he chose my family, and from among my father's sons he was pleased to make me king over all Israel. **5** From all the sons the LORD has given me — and he has given me many — he chose my son Solomon to sit on the throne of the LORD's kingdom over Israel.

**6** "God told me: 'Your son Solomon is the one who will build my house and my courts. I have chosen him as my son, and I will be his father. **7** I will make his kingdom last forever — if he remains determined to follow my commands and laws, as he does today.'

**8** "So now I charge you, in the sight of all Israel — the LORD's own assembly — and in the hearing of our God: be faithful to every command the LORD your God has given you, so that you may continue to possess this good land and pass it on to your descendants forever.

**9** "And you, my son Solomon — know the God of your father. Serve him wholeheartedly and with a willing spirit, for the LORD searches every heart and understands the motivation behind every thought. If you seek him, you will find him. But if you abandon him, he will reject you permanently.

**10** "Consider carefully: the LORD has chosen you to build a house as his sanctuary. Be strong, and get to work."

**11** Then David gave Solomon the plans for the temple complex — the portico, the main buildings, the treasuries, the upper rooms, the inner chambers, and the room for the atonement cover. **12** He gave him the plans for everything the Spirit had put in his mind — the courtyards surrounding the LORD's temple, all the side rooms, the storerooms of God's house, and the storerooms for the consecrated items.

**13** He also gave instructions about the priestly and Levitical divisions, all the work involved in serving at the LORD's temple, and every article used in worship there.

**14** He specified the weight of gold for every gold article used in each type of service, and the weight of silver for every silver article; **15** the weight for each gold lampstand and its lamps, and for each silver lampstand and its lamps, depending on the function of each; **16** the weight of gold for each table that held the sacred bread, and silver for the silver tables; **17** the weight of pure gold for the forks, sprinkling bowls, and pitchers; the weight for each gold dish and each silver dish;

**18** and the weight of refined gold for the incense altar. He also gave him the design for the golden chariot — the cherubim — whose wings were spread out, sheltering the ark of the LORD's covenant.

**19** "All of this," David said, "I have in writing from the LORD's own hand. He gave me understanding of every detail of the plan."

**20** David then told Solomon: "Be strong and courageous, and do the work. Don't be afraid or discouraged, because the LORD God — my God — is with you. He will not let you down or abandon you until every part of the work for the LORD's temple is finished.

**21** "The divisions of the priests and Levites are organized and ready for all the temple service. You will have willing, skilled workers for every task, and the officials and all the people are at your disposal."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 2 — "a resting place":** The temple is the end of a journey. Since Sinai, the ark had been a nomad, carried from camp to camp, captured by enemies, stored in homes. David's vision was to give God's presence on earth a permanent address. The word *menuchah* (rest) carries the weight of everything Israel longed for — settlement, peace, the end of wandering.

**Verse 9 — "know the God of your father":** David's charge to Solomon is not about theology but about relationship. "Know" (*da*) in Hebrew is intimate, personal, experiential. And the warning is stark: God can be found and God can be lost. The search is not guaranteed to last — it requires ongoing choice.

**Verse 18 — "the golden chariot — the cherubim":** This is the only verse in the Bible that calls the ark's cherubim a "chariot." The image is extraordinary — God rides above the ark on a golden chariot formed by the wings of angelic beings. This single word (*merkavah*) launched an entire tradition of Jewish mysticism.

**Verse 19 — "from the LORD's own hand":** David claims the blueprints are as divinely authored as the Ten Commandments. The temple plan is not architecture — it is revelation. Every measurement, every weight of gold, every room was specified by God himself, in writing. For the Chronicler, the temple is as authoritative as Torah.

*— PNEUMA*
